issues.description: [bug-hunt] Coach-chat macro_edit_request block crashes the ENTIRE chat when the LLM payload omits current_macros. src/components/blocks/MacroEditRequest.tsx dereferences data.current_macros.calories.target UNGUARDED in its useState initializer (lines 23-28) and again in currentValues (lines 50-55). Block data is untrusted LLM/backend output; EVERY sibling block guards this exact shape-drift class — MacroTargetCard.tsx uses (data.calories ?? z).target with the comment "a required nested object can be missing on shape drift ... instead of crashing the whole chat screen"; MicroTargetCard/MealSwapBlock/WorkoutPlanCard/MealPlanCard all normalize via Array.isArray/??. MacroEditRequest is the ONLY block that does not. InteractiveBlock.tsx has NO per-block ErrorBoundary (only Suspense for lazy-load) and there is no ErrorBoundary anywhere in src/components/coach or CoachChat.tsx, so the render throw propagates up and blanks the whole coach-chat view. EXPECTED: a partial/malformed macro_edit_request renders a degraded card (zeroed macros) like MacroTargetCard. ACTUAL: React render throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading calories)" (node-verified) → chat crashes. REPRO: coach emits a macro_edit_request block whose current_macros is null/missing (or whose current_macros.calories is missing) → chat view crashes on mount. Block is still registered (BLOCK_COMPONENTS line 42) though noted "replaced by meal_swap". FIX: default current_macros + each macro leaf to {target:0} mirroring MacroTargetCard z-guard, OR early-return a degraded card when current_macros is absent.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: MacroEditRequest.tsx dereferenced data.current_macros.<macro>.target unguarded (useState init + currentValues); a macro_edit_request block with missing/null current_macros threw on render and, with no per-block ErrorBoundary, blanked the whole coach-chat. Fix: mirror MacroTargetCard z-guard - default current_macros + each leaf to {target:0}, so a malformed payload renders a degraded zeroed card. Proof shows two shape-drift cases rendering without crash (top: current_macros missing -> all zeroed; bottom: calories leaf missing -> 0 cal, others intact). 30/30 unit tests green (2 new shape-drift regressions), tsc clean.

judge.note: Root-cause fix mirroring the established sibling-block z-guard pattern; minimal surgical change, 2 new shape-drift regression tests (30/30 green), tsc clean, real-render proof shows both drift cases degrade gracefully instead of crashing chat.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Canceling a friend request you SENT always fails with an "Unauthorized" error — the sent request can never be withdrawn.

Repro:
1. Go to /social/search, send a friend request to any user (they now see it as pending; you see it under Sent).
2. Open /social/friend-requests → Sent tab.
3. Tap Cancel on the request you sent.

Expected: the sent request is withdrawn and disappears from the Sent list.
Actual: a red toast "Couldn't cancel request — Unauthorized" appears and the request stays. It can NEVER be canceled from the app.

Root cause (cross-repo, confirmed by code trace):
- FE FriendRequests.tsx cancelMutation (Sent tab) calls socialService.rejectFriendRequest(friendship_id) -> POST /friends/reject/<id> (src/pages/FriendRequests.tsx:105-108, src/services/social.service.ts:134).
- Backend RejectFriendRequestResource (backend.py:10808-10810) authorizes ONLY the addressee: if friendship.addressee_id != user_id -> return 403 Unauthorized.
- But a SENT request has requester_id == current user (FriendRequestsSentResource filters requester_id==user_id, backend.py:10629-10632). The sender is the requester, never the addressee -> the addressee check fails -> 403 on every cancel.
- The Received-tab Reject works because there the current user IS the addressee. Only the Sent-tab Cancel is dead.

Fix: cancel a sent request via a route that authorizes the requester — e.g. FE cancelMutation should call socialService.unfriend(friendship_id) (DELETE /friends/<id>, backend UnfriendResource:10832-10834 already allows requester OR addressee), OR backend RejectFriendRequestResource should also permit friendship.requester_id == user_id (delete the pending row). Prefer the FE swap to unfriend for cancel.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: Sent-tab Cancel called POST /friends/reject/<id>, which RejectFriendRequestResource authorizes ONLY for the addressee; a sent request's current user is the requester, so it always 403'd 'Unauthorized' and could never be withdrawn. Fix: cancelMutation in src/pages/FriendRequests.tsx now calls socialService.unfriend (DELETE /friends/<id>) — UnfriendResource already permits requester OR addressee and deletes the pending row. Verified: mocked one pending sent request (QA acct has none live headless); network trace confirms Cancel now fires DELETE /api/v1/friends/<id> and the UI shows the 'Request cancelled' success toast (screenshot) instead of the red 'Couldn't cancel — Unauthorized'.

judge.note: Exact root cause fixed (addressee-only authz vs requester-sent request); minimal 1-line FE swap to the requester-authorized unfriend route; verified end-to-end via network trace (Cancel now fires DELETE /friends/<id>, not the 403 reject route) + success-toast screenshot. Not 100: live proof used a mocked sent request since the QA acct has no real pending sent request headless.

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Onboarding shows two DIFFERENT "Weekly pace" numbers for the same plan — the CoachPreview "Plan Created" card overstates the pace. Onboarding requires a target completion date (src/pages/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx:730). When it is set alongside a weight delta, calcOnboardingStats OVERRIDES weeklyChange to the required-to-hit-date rate (src/lib/onboarding-calc.ts:124-131) while keeping achievableWeeklyChange at the honest calorie-derived rate (onboarding-calc.ts:111). Owner ruling i-20260708-pc1a: every user-facing "Weekly pace" label MUST show the ACHIEVABLE rate. PostPlanTour (src/pages/onboarding/PostPlanTour.tsx:263-265) and PlanReadyOverview already comply, but Screen9_CoachPreview still reads the date-driven calc.weeklyChange for its user-facing pace: the "Plan Created" card "Weekly pace" row (src/pages/onboarding/Screen9_CoachPreview.tsx:1316-1318), the pace coach-notes (:557-561), the goal insight text (:777) and the debug summary line (:304). EXPECTED: CoachPreview and the immediately-following PostPlanTour show the SAME weekly pace = the pace the built calorie target actually delivers. ACTUAL: they disagree, and the card overstates a pace the plan cannot deliver — the exact defect pc1a fixed on the other two screens. REPRO (verified by replicating the calc): onboard as male, current 90kg -> goal 80kg, 180cm, 30yr, moderate activity. Built daily target = 2414 kcal which only delivers achievableWeeklyChange = 0.45 kg/wk. With a target date 10 weeks out, the "Plan Created" card shows "Weekly pace 1.0 kg/week" (date-driven 10kg/10wk); PostPlanTour hero shows "0.45 kg/week". With a 20-week date the card shows 0.50 vs 0.45. FIX: in Screen9_CoachPreview use calc.achievableWeeklyChange (not calc.weeklyChange) for ALL user-facing "Weekly pace" displays, matching PostPlanTour/PlanReadyOverview per pc1a.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: Screen9_CoachPreview read the date-driven calc.weeklyChange for its user-facing Weekly pace displays, which calcOnboardingStats overrides to the required-to-hit-date rate, overstating a pace the built calorie target cannot deliver (the defect owner ruling pc1a fixed on PostPlanTour/PlanReadyOverview). Fix: switched all 5 pace sites in Screen9_CoachPreview.tsx (Plan Created card row, coach notes, goal insight, build-animation safety validator, debug summary) to calc.achievableWeeklyChange. Verified via /dev/coach-preview: CoachPreview goal card and the following PostPlanTour hero now both show 0.45 kg/week (was 0.53 vs 0.45).

Verified end-to-end via /dev/coach-preview: CoachPreview goal card (-0.45) and following PostPlanTour hero (0.45 kg/week) now agree, the exact EXPECTED behavior; was 0.53 vs 0.45. issues.description: [bug-hunt] Challenge invitations cannot be accepted or declined — Join/Decline buttons never render. Social > Challenges is the only UI that calls joinChallenge/declineChallenge, and both buttons render only inside the isInvited branch (src/components/ChallengesView.tsx:451). isInvited is computed as challenge.my_status === "invited" (ChallengesView.tsx:376), but the backend challenge serializer _serialize_challenge (nyu_backend/backend.py:11056-11072) NEVER emits a my_status field (grep confirms zero occurrences of my_status in the backend). So challenge.my_status is undefined for every challenge => isInvited is always false. EXPECTED: a user invited to a friend’s challenge sees Join + Decline buttons. ACTUAL: they instead see the not-invited branch — a "Your Progress 0 / target" bar (ChallengesView.tsx:433) — and have no way to accept/decline; the invite is permanently un-actionable. REPRO: User A creates a challenge inviting friend B (backend adds B as participant status="invited", backend.py:11157). B opens Social > Challenges > Active. The card shows a progress bar and NO Join/Decline buttons. B is stuck. FIX: backend add "my_status" to _serialize_challenge (the current-user participant’s status); OR FE derive it from participants.find(p => p.user_id === currentUserId)?.status. NOTE backend participant status values are "accepted"/"invited"/"declined" (backend.py:11139/11157/11223), not "active" as the FE Challenge/Participant types assume (ChallengesView.tsx:11,27) — align both.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: Join/Decline only render inside the isInvited branch, but the backend challenge serializer never emitted the current user's own status (my_status), so it was always undefined and every invite showed a progress bar instead — permanently un-actionable. The FE status types also used 'active' where the backend uses 'accepted', and avatars read a non-existent 'user_name' key so they showed '?'. Fix: backend _serialize_challenge now returns my_status; the FE reads it (with a participants[] fallback), aligns the status union to accepted/invited/declined/completed, and reads the 'name' key. An invited challenge now shows working Join + Decline buttons and real participant avatars.

judge.note: Recaptured Challenges>Active: invited card shows Join+Decline (no progress bar) and R/Y avatars; backend deployed + FE tests pass

issues.description: [bug-hunt] "Started a challenge" activity-feed events are silently dropped and never shown. When a challenge is created the backend writes an ActivityFeedEvent with event_type="challenge_created" (nyu_backend/backend.py:11167) and the /social/activity-feed endpoint serves it to friends (backend.py:11329-11353). But ActivityFeedView filters events to only those present in EVENT_CONFIG (src/components/ActivityFeedView.tsx:75-77), and EVENT_CONFIG (ActivityFeedView.tsx:56-64) + EVENT_LABEL (:17-25) have NO "challenge_created" entry => every such event is filtered out. EXPECTED: a friend creating a challenge shows "Started a challenge: X" in the feed (backend comment at backend.py:11165 states the description key "is what the frontend feed renders", i.e. it was meant to display). ACTUAL: the event is persisted to the DB but never rendered for anyone. REPRO: A and B are friends. A creates any challenge. B opens Social > Activity feed — the challenge_created event is absent. FIX: add "challenge_created" to EVENT_CONFIG (e.g. Trophy icon) and EVENT_LABEL ("started a challenge") in ActivityFeedView.tsx; eventText() already returns data.description so the copy will render.

fix.description: Root cause: when a friend creates a challenge the backend logs a 'challenge_created' activity-feed event, but ActivityFeedView only renders event types present in EVENT_CONFIG and this type was missing from EVENT_LABEL + EVENT_CONFIG, so every such row was persisted yet silently filtered out. issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Coach-chat grocery list renders BLANK category headers (Produce / Dairy / etc. section titles are empty).

Root cause (full-stack field-name contract mismatch):
- Backend tool schema `show_grocery_list` (nyu_backend/app/services/coach_tools.py:332-352) defines each category object with the property `category_name`.
- The block payload is the LLM tool-call arguments passed through VERBATIM by response_parser.py — both the non-streaming path (parse_openai_response, line ~179-185) and the streaming path (parse_streaming_response, line ~265-271) do `"data": data` with NO grocery normalization. Only `meal_logger` gets a field remap (`suggested_foods`->`suggestions`, lines 163-177); grocery was never given the equivalent.
- The frontend expects `name`: type `GroceryCategory.name` (src/components/blocks/types.ts:238) and GroceryListBlock renders the section header as `{cat.name}` (src/components/blocks/GroceryListBlock.tsx:157). The normalizer at GroceryListBlock.tsx:67-72 spreads `...cat` but never maps `category_name`->`name`.

So a schema-compliant coach tool call emits `{category_name, items:[...]}`, the block reads `cat.name` = undefined, and every category `<h4>` header renders empty — the grocery list looks like ungrouped items under blank titles.

This is the SAME class as the already-fixed `suggested_foods`->`suggestions` mismatch (which was normalized for meal_logger in response_parser); grocery_list was missed. NOTE: distinct from tick #44 c7a3 (that was the standalone /shopping-list PAGE serializer) and from the tick #23 GroceryListBlock check-state-reset / currency-cosmetic notes.

Expected: each grocery category section shows its name (Produce, Dairy, Grains, ...).
Actual: category header text is blank for every section.

Repro: 1) Open Coach Chat (/coach-chat). 2) Ask the coach to show your grocery list (fires the `show_grocery_list` tool). 3) The rendered grocery block shows category sections with empty headers above the items.

Fix (pick one): normalize `category_name`->`name` for `grocery_list` in response_parser.py (both paths, mirroring the meal_logger precedent); OR rename the tool schema property to `name`; OR read `cat.category_name ?? cat.name` in GroceryListBlock + the type. Related (not filed): the block also carries no `id`, so per-item checkbox toggles never persist (GroceryListBlock.tsx:109 `if (data.id)` is always false) — appears intentional (checks are local UI), noted for context only.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] "My Group" leaderboard silently drops any partner-group member ranked outside the global top 50 (and hides your own rank card if you are below #50 globally).

Root cause (src/components/LeaderboardView.tsx): the board is built from a SINGLE call to leaderboardService.getLeaderboard(selectedType, selectedPeriod) at line 96, which uses the service defaults page=1, limit=50 and sends NO group parameter — so it returns only the GLOBAL top 50. The "My Group" tab is then produced (line 207-213) by intersecting those 50 rows with the partner-group member IDs (groupMemberIds) and re-ranking 1..n. There is no other query that fetches group members' scores/streaks. partnerGroups only supplies member IDs, not scores.

Consequence: a partner-group member whose global rank is > 50 (very common with any real user base) never appears on "My Group". Worse, currentUserRankCard (line 221-228) in group scope is derived from groupResults.find(e=>e.is_current_user); if the current user is ranked > 50 globally, they are absent from the 50 rows, so me is undefined -> the "Your Rank" card is hidden, and if none of the group is in the top 50 the tab shows the empty state "No group members on this board yet" even though the group is active. The inline comment at line 189-190 claims this "works correctly today" — it does not for the common below-top-50 case.

Expected: My Group ranks ALL members of the group against each other regardless of global rank; your own group rank always shows.
Actual: only members who happen to sit in the global top 50 are shown; everyone else (often including you) vanishes.

Repro: 1) Be in a partner group. 2) Ensure you (or a group member) are ranked below #50 on the global board for the selected type (e.g. wellness_streak / all_time on a populated board). 3) Social -> Leaderboard -> tap "My Group". Observe missing members and/or missing "Your Rank" card / empty-state despite an active group.

Fix: pass a group filter to the /leaderboards endpoint (backend-side member filtering) OR fetch each group member's score and rank the full member set client-side, instead of intersecting the global top-50 page.
